about.tool: A broad-edged pen held at about 35°.
about.slant: About 10°, the same for every letter.
about.proportions: x-height about 5¼ nib widths; ascenders and descenders one x-height more each (ascender line at 2, descender at 1); capitals 1.4 x-heights.
about.features: Compressed and springing: the arches of n, m, h, b, p, r leave the stem about two thirds up and turn at the top right; a, d, g, q, u are the same shape the other way up (round at the bottom left, a hairline back up into the stem), with a separate hairline top. Small wedge heads, hairline exits, and long tails on f, g, j, y finished from the left. The capitals are swash capitals: wide, begun with a thick entry swash from a curl at the left, many with a sweeping foot. Simplified: the joins between letters are not drawn; the figures (the sheet has none) are the old-style figures of the writing books.
about.history: The chancery hand (cancelleresca) of the papal scribes in Renaissance Italy; Ludovico degli Arrighi's La Operina (1522) is its classic manual. Revived in the 20th century by Edward Johnston and Alfred Fairbank.
